# Prioritized Roadmap — Build the Foundation Before the Fireworks

The Awtsmoos gives infinite possibility, but vessels reveal it in order; Awtsmoos.com should harden the covenant first, then widen every creative border.

## P0 — Make the current core trustworthy
1. Fix public exports: export `createMoviePromptIntent` and all intended AI/runtime APIs from one canonical index.
2. Fix `aiMovieContract()` to derive protocol/version from a real capability profile or protocol constants.
3. Replace compact one-line source patterns with fully readable modular formatting.
4. Define a formal JSON schema or equivalent typed validation contract.
5. Validate layer end time, keyframes, cameras, transitions, cast IDs, asset IDs, references and payload shapes.
6. Add canonical error codes and warnings, not only free-form strings.
7. Decide which Animator adapter is authoritative and deprecate/bridge the duplicate.
8. Make every adapter return `{projection, report, capabilities, canonicalMovie}` consistently.
9. Add adapter round-trip tests and explicit loss accounting.
10. Add protocol version migrations before v1 spreads further.
11. Add tests under `apps/shared/movie/tests` for protocol, AI, runtime, adapters and 180-second movie.
12. Track the canonical core in Git and document it as the sole source of truth.

## P1 — Make AI genuinely direct movies
13. Introduce a provider interface: `planMovie`, `reviseMovie`, `generateAssetBrief`, `reviewMovie`.
14. Separate deterministic fallback prompt parsing from real model intelligence.
15. Add hierarchical planning: movie -> acts -> scenes -> shots -> layers -> keyframes.
16. Add a canonical patch language so AI revisions change only what was requested.
17. Add duration/pacing solver and narration/dialogue timing constraints.
18. Add continuity state and a character/cast bible.
19. Add self-critique passes for repetition, pacing, legibility and unsupported capabilities.
20. Store AI provenance and prompts in metadata without polluting renderer semantics.

## P2 — Complete semantic media vocabulary
21. Add audio, dialogue, narration, music, ambience, SFX and caption layer/track types.
22. Add video/image/media asset layers.
23. Add mask, matte, adjustment and compositing semantics.
24. Add camera tracks separate from ordinary layers.
25. Add parent/group/constraint semantics and reusable symbols.
26. Add data sources for charts/diagrams/tutorials.
27. Add semantic character pose, gaze, gesture, emotion and lipsync tracks.

## P3 — Professional 2D and 3D engines
28. 2D: bezier editor, masks, blend modes, path morphing, text animators and graph editor.
29. 3D: real meshes/materials/lights/cameras with PBR and shadows.
30. Rigging/IK and animation blending for characters.
31. Physics and procedural particles with deterministic seeds.
32. Proper camera lens/focus/DOF and cinematic motion systems.
33. Post-processing/color pipeline.
34. Renderer abstraction allowing Canvas proof, WebGL/WebGPU spatial preview and headless export.

## P4 — Editing experience
35. One shared timeline interaction model: snapping, trims, ripple, markers, nesting and keyframe graph.
36. Shared command/undo layer so human and AI edits are equally reversible.
37. Storyboard/shot-list view synchronized with timeline and canvas.
38. Beginner/Expert modes over the same project data.
39. Full mobile interaction design with bottom sheets, gestures and safe-area-aware previews.
40. Voice editing and contextual AI actions.

## P5 — Reliability and scale
41. Asset registry, hashing, proxy/original relationships and missing-file diagnostics.
42. Autosave, version snapshots, recovery and project integrity checks.
43. Render queue, cancellation, retries and resumable final export.
44. OffscreenCanvas/workers, frame caches and adaptive preview quality.
45. WebCodecs plus ffmpeg/headless compatibility matrix.
46. Performance budgets for low-end phones and large 3-minute+ projects.
47. Deterministic render manifests and frame hashes.
48. Golden visual tests across scene timestamps.
49. Fuzz tests for AI-generated malformed movie JSON.
50. Cross-browser/mobile E2E tests.

## P6 — Product-level magic
51. Templates that remain fully editable after AI generation.
52. Automatic cutdowns: 16:9 master -> 9:16 short -> 1:1 social.
53. Multilingual dubbing/captions with timing preservation.
54. Automatic B-roll and infographic suggestions.
55. Review mode with comments and AI-addressable notes.
56. Educational factuality/citation metadata where appropriate.
57. Project/plugin SDK so new app personalities can join the protocol cleanly.
58. Capability negotiation for third-party renderers/editors.
59. Import/export bridges for common standards where feasible.
60. A true acceptance movie suite: narrative + tutorial + infographic + people + particles + camera work + 2D + 3D + audio, rendered for three real minutes and probed/sampled automatically.

## Definition of excellent
A user should be able to say: "Make a three-minute film teaching this concept, with two recurring characters, animated charts, a 3D world, text callouts and cinematic cameras," receive an editable structured movie, revise any part conversationally, open the same project in multiple specialized apps without losing unsupported semantics, and export measured real media from a phone or desktop.
